title: Rating Reduction Notice Periods and Protection Periods for Disability Compensation
content:
**Figures governing a proposed reduction of a Disability Compensation rating** (identical at every tier, Disability Compensation (10% Combined Rating) through Disability Compensation (100% Combined Rating)):

| Period | Figure |
|---|---|
| Evidence period after the proposed-reduction notice | 60 calendar days from the notice date |
| Predetermination hearing request that holds the current rate | Received not later than 30 calendar days after the date of the proposed reduction notice |
| Period after notice of the final reduction decision | 60 calendar days; the reduction takes effect the last day of the month in which they expire |
| Protected rating | A rating continuously in effect for 20 years or more is not reduced below that level except for fraud |
| Stabilized rating | A rating in effect for 5 years or more is reduced only on a full examination showing sustained material improvement |
| Routine future examinations | Not scheduled for a veteran aged 55 or older |

**Illustrations (hypothetical)**

- A proposed-reduction notice dated 2 March 2026: the evidence period runs through 1 May 2026 (60 days counted from 3 March), and the last day a hearing request holds the current rate is 1 April 2026, the notice date plus 30 days.
- Notice of a final reduction decision dated 10 June 2026: 60 calendar days expire on 9 August 2026, so the reduction takes effect on 31 August 2026.
- A rating in effect continuously for 19 years is not yet protected at the 20-year mark; at 20 years it is.
- A veteran aged 54 can be scheduled for a routine future examination; a veteran aged 55 is not.
